newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait index up, trade down ahead of debt deadline.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait index up, trade down ahead of debt deadline.

text.p: Kuwait Stock Exchange shares index rose 0.8 in the week to Wednesday while trade fell ahead of a September 6 deadline for bad debt payments by private debtors.
"The (volume) fall is normal after big rises. Some of it could be due to debt payments next week," Ahmad Khalaf al-Najar, a dealer at the Kuwait Investment Company, said.
Private debtors involved in a programme to settle $20 billion of bad debt owed to the state have to pay a portion of the debt in the first week of September.
The exchange did not witness remarkable sales ahead of a previous payment of the debt owed by private investors and companies including some listed firms.

"The market will be much stronger in the second week of September after the bad debt payment and when many dealers finish their holidays," said Khaled al-Saleh, chairman of the Gulf Brokerage Company.

"The debt payment will not have much effect on the market. It is only psychological. The market is very good, look at the prices," said Saleh. "One share or two could be affected but the market will not be."
Dealers said the decline in volume was a normal development after rising for a few consecutive weeks.
"If the market keeps going up that would cause a crisis," said Najar. "The market will rise again. People will start soon to buy selected shares to collect the dividend after the end of the year."
Many listed shares reported healthy profits in the first half of 1996. Announcements spurred active trade in past weeks.
"Strong shares like Kuwait Finance House (KFH) are expected to rise further. There is talk that the House will have big profits this year," said a dealer. KFH rose 40 fils or 6.5 percent this week.
The official index rose 13.2 points to 1,623.4. Gains led losses 20-18, with 13 stocks unchanged.
Daily average volume fell 26.6 percent to 71.7 million shares, with a total volume of 358.5 million shares.
Traded value eased 17.7 percent on a daily average basis to 14.4 million dinars ($48.1 million), with a total value of 72 million. Contracts fell 14.7 percent to an average of 950 a day.
The most active stocks were Commercial Bank, Kuwait Real Estate Bank, Investment Projects, United Realty, Pearl of Kuwait Real Estate and National Investment.

The property sector was the most active sector by value with 28.3 percent, followed by investment with 26.5 percent and banks with 23.9 percent. Properties were also the most active by volume with 37.8 percent. Investment came second with 32 percent and banks were third with 14.8 percent.
